title: Why This, Not That? Mining User Profiles for Pair-wise Counterfactuals
abstract: arXiv:2608.21662v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The topic of explanation in recommender systems has seen steady research attention since the earliest days of the field. With some exceptions, this work has focused on the explanation of single items in a recommendation list and, especially recently, has emphasized approaches that are decoupled from the logic of the recommendation algorithm itself. Based on findings in the psychology of interpersonal communication, we propose a new task, pairwise interpretation of item rankings, asking the comparative question ``Why is item A ranked higher than item B?''. An effective solution to this task, we argue, is inherently grounded in the operation of the recommendation algorithm. We propose a class of techniques based on counterfactual learning to uncover the items in a user's profile that have contributed to the relative ranking of items. translated_title: 为何此物而非彼物？挖掘用户画像以实现成对反事实解释
translated_abstract: 自推荐系统领域诞生之初，关于解释的研究就一直受到持续关注。除少数例外，这些工作主要聚焦于推荐列表中单个项目的解释，并且近年来特别强调与推荐算法逻辑本身脱钩的方法。基于人际沟通心理学的研究发现，我们提出了一项新任务，即对物品排名的成对解释，提出比较性问题：“为何物品A排名高于物品B？”我们认为，有效解决该任务的方法本质上应植根于推荐算法的操作。我们提出了一类基于反事实学习的技术，以揭示用户画像中对物品相对排名有贡献的项目。通过使用多个数据集，我们证明了能够识别出此类项目，作为比较性解释的潜在基础。
tldr: 本文提出了一项新任务——成对解释物品排名（“为何A高于B？”），并基于反事实学习开发了一种方法，能够识别用户画像中影响相对排名的关键项目，从而实现与推荐算法逻辑紧密耦合的解释。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a new task of pairwise item ranking interpretation (“Why is A ranked higher than B?”) and develops a counterfactual learning-based method to identify key user-profile items influencing relative rankings, yielding explanations tightly coupled with the recommendation algorithm's logic.
